job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today we are exploring symmetry. Look at this regular pentagon. How many lines of symmetry does it have? Rohan: I think it only has one vertical line of symmetry because that is how we usually draw it. Teacher: Actually, a regular pentagon has five lines of symmetry, one through each vertex. Symmetry isn't just about vertical lines; it can be horizontal or diagonal too. Priya: Does that mean a mirror image is always identical to the original object? Teacher: Not quite. If you look at the letter 'P' in a mirror, it flips horizontally, so it looks different from the original. Symmetry means the shape remains unchanged after an operation. Rohan: What about rotational symmetry? Does a shape only have it if we rotate it a full 360 degrees? Teacher: No, that would be trivial because everything looks the same after a full circle. Rotational symmetry means the shape looks identical after a rotation of less than 360 degrees. For example, a square looks the same after a 90-degree turn. Priya: So, symmetry is about how shapes behave when we flip or turn them, not just how they look when standing still.

items.evidence: Actually, a regular pentagon has five lines of symmetry, one through each vertex.
items.q: Rohan folds a paper regular pentagon so both halves match. How many such folds are possible?
options: Two, one upright and one flat
Ten, one per side and corner
items.explain: A regular pentagon has five lines of symmetry, one through each vertex, not just one.

thinks a horizontal line must come with a vertical one

items.q: A shape's only line of symmetry is slanted, from corner to corner. What can we say about it?
options: It still counts as a symmetrical shape
It is not symmetrical, as the line is slanted
It is symmetrical only if a vertical line exists
It is symmetrical only when redrawn standing upright
items.explain: Lines of symmetry can be vertical, horizontal or diagonal, so a slanted line still counts.

wrong.why: thinks only vertical lines count as symmetry
thinks other lines need a vertical line too
thinks the drawing's position decides symmetry

items.evidence: If you look at the letter 'P' in a mirror, it flips horizontally, so it looks different from the original.
items.q: Priya holds a card with the letter 'P' up to a mirror. What will she see?
options: A reversed P that looks different
An exact copy of the original P
A P unchanged, since P is symmetrical
items.explain: In a mirror, P flips horizontally, so its image looks different from the original.

wrong.why: thinks a mirror image is identical to the object

items.q: Why is a full 360-degree turn not used to test for rotational symmetry?
